newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's Mobutu has fresh round of health checks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu has fresh round of health checks.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, who underwent surgery last year for prostate cancer, was given medical tests in Monaco on Saturday and could return to his troubled country before the beginning of February, an aide said.
"He underwent a series of routine medical tests, as would be expected after surgery," Mobutu Nzanga, the president's communications director, told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"He is going to be returning to Zaire in the next few days -- quite soon. As soon as the doctors set the date of his return, we will announce it to the press," Nzanga said. "I think that should take place before the beginning of the month of February."

Mobutu, who has been recuperating at his palatial Riviera villa in southern France, underwent a similar series of tests in Monaco last weekend after spending three weeks in Zaire, where Tutsi-led rebels have seized territory in the east.
Nzanga said the medical tests were a normal part of the follow-up of any patient following cancer therapy.

"He has his health, and that is what is important," he said when asked if Mobutu were in good health. He said the president had not really had time to recuperate because his convalesence was constantly being interrupted by meetings and official visits.
Doctors in Switzerland operated on Mobutu in August last year, but Nzanga denied that Mobutu had undergone minor surgery last weekend in Monaco, as reported by French radio at the time.
"He did not have surgery," he said.

Mobutu was given the latest round of tests at Monaco's Princess Grace Hospital on Saturday morning and afterwards returned to his villa in the Riviera town of Roquebrune- Cap-Martin, Nzanga said. The hospital declined all comment.
Mobutu's stay in southern France was his second in recent months following his operation in Switzerland last August.
While in Zaire in December, Mobutu carried out a major reshuffle in the government and the army high command in preparation for an intended counter-attack on rebel positions.
The rebels have vowed to march to Kinshasa to overthrow the president, who has ruled the mineral-rich country for 31 years.
